## Design

### 2026-10-31: I spent some time researching whether I should use OLED or TFT, but it seemed that OLED was easier since it had just 4 pins instead of 7 on the TFT. I used the guide and added the 1x4 connector and so

**6h**

I spent some time researching whether I should use OLED or TFT, but it seemed that OLED was easier since it had just 4 pins instead of 7 on the TFT. I used the guide and added the 1x4 connector and some other items to the schematics. I decided to add the second 1x4 connector for the I2C sensors because I would have one in case I ever decide that I want a sensor. I hadn't really thought of what I wanted to make at this point.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/d9343212885c8c65d97ac633ad16c693c5c899634938bdfd921d9b45c341a167.png)

I added the footprints and started making the PCB. I wanted the SCL and SDA in the front and a GND pour at the back.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/d04ac79262a6fd9894684304e7ddb0148cd0c653b87b2e72f9addecb6a729a53.png)

Everything was simple enough, but I didn't know how to make a GND fill, so I had to research. For some reason, none of the instructions I saw told me that I had to press "b" to actually fill it, until I saw this video:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 183849](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/1980392bee87e283cba1c77033aecadac7a9d7f837ec08b96aa7087e86f32d52.png)

After I did that, I started thinking about what I actually wanted to make. I decided that I wanted something fun, like games. However, for fast graphics, I would have needed an SPI OLED, so I thought that I could have slow games like 2048, but I don't know for sure. I thought about what I would use as an input, and I thought tactile switches would be good since I didn't want to take up too much space with key switches. I found one that was 6x6x7.3, which seemed like a good size.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/8bd9412ca10803193e6e9cc769ce1fc030e2607dc14c6ff5218509a1458ca3b6.png)

Then I had to add them to the schematics and PCB, and I wired one side of each to GND and the other to GPIOs. I made 5 buttons in total: up, down, left, right, and enter/select.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 221626](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/700db72062088230613487f69bde84ead8e2a043c3b00b547cc87b2fd4f69b94.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/df8c3aa462f8c083819089e733fa48c9c8ef561e6c6a401721730d3fe484a2ef.png)

I then added them to the PCB, and I wanted to use the keyboard arrow-key style for the directional buttons. I added the "select" one to the side, but it was a bit awkward-looking.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/f82651574ae938f3bdd8d3301a2b04894dbbe19679f2653444b51805c536950d.png)

### 2026-11-01: I wanted to see how the buttons would fit overall, and I measured an actual keyboard's arrow keys. I was very off, so I moved them farther apart and put the select button on the other side of the PCB.

**6h**

I wanted to see how the buttons would fit overall, and I measured an actual keyboard's arrow keys. I was very off, so I moved them farther apart and put the select button on the other side of the PCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/3d2dbabcdc86baa526f74c8476398c48101173838754743cf3ea80737c63bcb9.png)

I started thinking about which games I wanted and searched the web for ideas. Then, coincidentally, I found a repository on GitHub for a Raspberry Pi Pico OLED retro gaming system.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/ab2f35d1c46b4321a484ffc44d8911b2af0dfdc92d5b1b6387bc2590f9b8333c.png)

I was  very happy that I found the repo, and I looked around. I saw that he had used a piezo buzzer for sound effects, and I thought that I would like one too. I added it to the schematics and expanded the edge cuts in the PCB so I could insert it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/2b2b10998064005a7c22317654faf05b320330a3cd6c3e04b94c40444ca43839.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/0458d63c3197ebbd6a52d2b38b7888b6f0e9c6a7a8f597b73debf0eb111a18f9.png)

I then added a silkscreen footprint with my initials, which I made for the MIDI keyboard in week three.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 162322](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/56f796667e284ebc46f4c393b2c6d1acd0e690901857a1710f2d6fdeb3cbcd3e.png)

I also moved my JST SH pin connector to the side and rewired it so it fits better.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 163104](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/b74c94e328db35bfbbed683bd966effabf2f8999d9aea44696450df2e1942359.png)

I then started getting my parts for the BOM. I had to get pretty much everything from AliExpress and Digi-Key because the other options were not cheap enough.
